question: 'Waiting for a Visa' is a 20-page autobiography of ________________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **"Waiting for a Visa"** is a 20-page autobiography written by **Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar**, one of India's most eminent social reformers.
 
• This autobiography was written between **1935 and 1936**, and it serves as a personal account of Dr Ambedkar's experiences with caste-based discrimination.
 
• The work is considered an **educational document** and is part of the Columbia University syllabus for its insights into social issues.
 
• It highlights the challenges faced by marginalized communities in pre-independence India and Dr Ambedkar’s efforts to combat social injustice.
 
• Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar is also known as the **architect of the Indian Constitution** and the leader of the Dalit movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar:**

 
 
• He was born on **14 April 1891** in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, and belonged to the Mahar caste, a Dalit community.
 
• He earned a doctorate from **Columbia University** and a D.Sc. from the London School of Economics.
 
• He played a pivotal role in drafting the **Constitution of India** and was the first Law Minister of independent India.
 
• Ambedkar converted to Buddhism in 1956, along with millions of his followers, as a rejection of caste-based discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Significance of "Waiting for a Visa":**
 
 
• The book is a firsthand account of casteism in India and provides insights into the social fabric of that time.
 
• It is a valuable resource for understanding the plight of Dalits and the systemic discrimination they faced.
 
• The narrative is both autobiographical and a call for social reform.
 
 
 
• **Dr Ambedkar’s Contributions:**
 
 
• He fought for the rights of the untouchables and worked to abolish the caste system.
 
• He founded the **Independent Labour Party** in 1936 and later the **Scheduled Castes Federation**.
 
• He was instrumental in the formation of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) based on his economic thesis.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Dr Ambedkar is celebrated annually on **Ambedkar Jayanti**, observed on 14th April.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in 1990.
 
• His writings and speeches continue to inspire movements for social justice and equality worldwide.
